'''Reinhold Strassmann''' (or '''Straßmann''') (24 January 1893 in Berlin – late October 1944 in [[Auschwitz concentration camp]]) was a German mathematician who proved [[Strassmann's theorem]]. His Ph.D. advisor at [[University of Marburg]] was [[Kurt Hensel]].

Born into a [[Jewish]] family,<ref>Burkhard Madea, ''History of Forensic Medicine'', Lehmanns Media (2017), p. 148</ref> Strassmann refused to leave [[Nazi Germany]], and he was eventually detained and deported to [[Theresienstadt concentration camp]] in 1943. On October 23, 1944, he was deported from Theresienstadt to [[Auschwitz concentration camp]], where he was murdered soon after.<ref>[http://109.123.214.108/en/victims/PERSON.ITI.663261 Reinhold Strassmann's record] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150715031028/http://109.123.214.108/en/victims/PERSON.ITI.663261 |date=2015-07-15 }} in the Victims Database at {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140717233158/http://109.123.214.108/|title=holocaust.cz}}</ref>

He was the son of the forensic pathologist [[Fritz Strassmann (physician)|Fritz Strassmann]].
